newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch say German "mad cow" import was healthy.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say German "mad cow" import was healthy.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Wednesday a cow imported into the Netherlands with suspected mad cow disease entered the food chain in 1995 but insisted the animal was healthy at the time of slaughtering.

"The animal was checked three times -- when it was exported from Germany, when it was imported into the Netherlands and just before slaughtering. It was healthy," ANP news agency quoted Dutch farm minister Jozias van Aartsen as saying.

A nationwide hunt for the animal was sparked by confirmation on Tuesday of the first cow born in Germany with the disease. Dutch farm officials said they had been informed that the mother of the cow was probably exported to the Netherlands in 1995.
Officials traced details of the Galloway cow but said it had been slaughtered in August 1995 and the meat sold off as normal.
Van Aartsen insisted checks were sufficient for there to be no danger to public health.
The minister also said the cow had produced one calf, which had not yet entered the food chain. This calf would be killed and taken to a scientific laboratory for inspection, he added.

The German cow, the country's fifth case of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) but the first born there to die of the disease, was calf to a Galloway cow imported from Britain. It was this animal, as part of a herd of 39 Galloways, that Germany believes was then exported to the Netherlands.

Earlier on Wednesday, Germany announced that all cattle imported from Britain and Switzerland would be culled to calm public fears. The state secretary at the German Agriculture Ministry said the decision would affect 2,600 cattle from Britain and 2,600 from Switzerland.
In April last year the Dutch began the slaughter of 64,000 imported British calves over fears of mad cow disease.
